questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the quantity of matter present in an object?
questions.solution: Mass is the term used to describe the quantity of matter present in an object. Weight is a measure of the force of gravity acting on an object, volume is the space an object occupies, and density is the amount of mass in a given volume.

questions.stem: If you add more salt to a solution that already contains dissolved salt, what will happen if the solution is saturated?
choices: The salt will continue to dissolve completely
The salt will start to dissolve partially
The salt will not dissolve and settle at the bottom
questions.solution: A saturated solution is one in which the maximum amount of solute has already been dissolved. Adding more salt to such a solution will not cause it to dissolve further, so it will remain as solid at the bottom. The other options are incorrect because they suggest dissolution or evaporation, which do not occur in a saturated solution.

questions.stem: A student dissolves 10 g of sugar in 50 mL of water. What is the solubility of sugar in water based on this?
questions.solution: Solubility is defined as the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in 100 mL of solvent. If 10 g of sugar dissolves in 50 mL, then 20 g would dissolve in 100 mL, making 20 g per 100 mL the correct answer. The other options are incorrect calculations based on the given data.

hi.stem: एक छात्र 50 मिली जल में 10 ग्राम चीनी को घोलता है। इसके आधार पर जल में चीनी की विलेयता क्या है?
hi.solution: विलेयता की परिभाषा विलायक में घुल सकने वाले विलेय की अधिकतम मात्रा है। यदि 10 ग्राम चीनी 50 मिली में घुल जाती है, तो 100 मिली में 20 ग्राम घुल सकती है, जिसके कारण 20 ग्राम प्रति 100 मिली सही उत्तर है। अन्य विकल्प दिए गए आंकड़ों पर आधारित गलत गणनाएं हैं।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation accurately reflects the English content with appropriate scientific terminology and maintains the same answer structure.

mr.stem: एका विद्यार्थ्याने 50 मिली पाण्यात 10 ग्रॅम चीनी विरघळवली. या आधारावर पाण्यात चीनीची विलेयता किती आहे?
mr.solution: विलेयता ही विलायकात विरघळू शकणारा विलेयाचा अधिकतम प्रमाण असतो. जर 50 मिली मध्ये 10 ग्रॅम चीनी विरघळली असेल, तर 100 मिली मध्ये 20 ग्रॅम विरघळेल, ज्यामुळे 20 ग्रॅम प्रति 100 मिली हे बरोबर उत्तर असते. इतर उत्तरे दिलेल्या आकडेवारीवर आधारित चुकीच्या गणना आहेत.

questions.stem: What does the label '1 litre' on a packet of oil indicate?
choices: It indicates the volume of the oil
It indicates the mass of the oil
It indicates the density of the oil
It indicates the weight of the oil
questions.solution: The label '1 litre' refers to the amount of space the oil occupies, which is its volume. Mass and weight are different properties that depend on the amount of matter and gravity, respectively. Density is mass per unit volume, so it is not directly indicated by the volume alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate way to measure 70 mL of water?
choices: Using a 50 mL measuring cylinder twice
Using a 100 mL measuring cylinder once
Using a 250 mL measuring cylinder once
Using a 500 mL measuring cylinder once
questions.solution: Using a 100 mL measuring cylinder once is the most accurate because it is the closest size to 70 mL, allowing for a single, precise measurement. Using a smaller cylinder like 50 mL would require two measurements, increasing the chance of error. Larger cylinders, such as 250 mL or 500 mL, would make it harder to read the exact volume due to the larger scale, reducing accuracy.

questions.stem: A student adds salt to water and notices that after some time, the salt no longer dissolves and settles at the bottom. What does this indicate about the solution?
questions.solution: When salt stops dissolving and settles at the bottom, it means the solution has reached its maximum capacity to dissolve the salt. This is the definition of a saturated solution. An unsaturated solution would still be able to dissolve more salt, a concentrated solution refers to the amount of solute, and a dilute solution has very little solute, none of which match the observed behavior.

questions.stem: A student added 20 g of salt to 100 mL of water at room temperature and found that not all the salt dissolved. What can be concluded from this observation?
questions.solution: A saturated solution is one in which no more solute can be dissolved at a given temperature. Since not all the salt dissolved, the solution has reached its maximum capacity for dissolving salt, making it a saturated solution. The other options describe different states of solutions that do not match the given situation. An unsaturated solution would allow more salt to dissolve, a supersaturated solution would have more solute than normally possible, and a colloid is not a solution.
